title: The Sacred Laws of the Âryas, Part II: Vâsishtha and Baudhâyana
altTitles: Sacred Laws of the Aryas II
Sacred Books of the East, vol. 14
attributionNote: The sutras are ascribed to the sages Vasishtha and Baudhayana and belong to their schools. Both texts are composite, and the Vasishtha recension in particular has absorbed later metrical material.
description: The second volume of the Sacred Laws completes Bühler's dharmasutras with Vasishtha and Baudhayana. Vasishtha is a compact treatise in thirty chapters on the sources of law, the duties of the king, purity, women, inheritance, homicide and penance, much of it in verse and close in substance to Manu. Baudhayana is the longest of the dharmasutras, covering the sacred student's training, the householder's rites, the law of evidence and debt, and an elaborate system of penances.
historicalContext: Vasishtha and Baudhayana stand at the end of the dharmasutra tradition and show the transition to the metrical smritis. Bühler's translation appeared in 1882 as SBE 14, completing the corpus of dharmasutras begun in SBE 2.
availabilityNote: Complete. Vasishtha's and Baudhayana's law sutras with Bühler's introduction and notes are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed chapter (prasna) per chapter. The volume's title page, contents and index are not part of the work.
